Is the phone your child's babysitter? Simple family rules for healthy young eyes.

• Close-up screens keep the eye's focusing muscle tight, and children blink less: tired, dry eyes
• Studies show outdoor play in daylight lowers children's risk of short sight
• Do: screens at arm's length, 20-20-20 breaks, screens off an hour before bed
• Don't: screens for babies and toddlers, phones in a dark room, screens at meals
• Make family screen-free time; kids copy what we do
• Watch for squinting, sitting close to the TV, eye rubbing or headaches; children often don't complain

gmb.text: Simple screen rules for healthy young eyes. When children stare at screens up close for long, the focusing muscle inside the eye stays tight and they blink less, which leads to tired, dry eyes. Studies show that children who play outdoors in daylight are less likely to become short-sighted. Do: keep screens at arm's length, look at something far away for 20 seconds every 20 minutes, and switch screens off an hour before bed. Don't: give screens to babies and toddlers, let children use phones in a dark room, or keep screens on at meals. Make family screen-free time for books, games and play. If your child squints, sits close to the TV, rubs their eyes or gets headaches, book an eye test. Book an eye test on WhatsApp: 044 4356 9998
